title: FileDialog's OK button has odd handling
body: ### Tested versions 4.6 rc1 ### System information W10 ### Issue description I noticed FileDialog will sometimes disable its OK (Open/Save etc.) button, but it's done inconsistently and it does not indicate whether the dialog can be accepted. All of these invalid states are possible: - [x] The file dialog has a correct file selected and correct path. Open button is disabled, but you can press Enter to accept. - (this is actually a regression in 4.6, but not important. It's caused by a file being selected by default, while previously it was not the case.) - There is no file selected, but the path is correct. Open is disabled, Enter still works. - A file is selected, but the path points to non-existent file. Open is enabled, but pressing it does nothing, Enter does nothing. This is caused by the discrepancy between OK button checks and accept checks. - OK button is enabled based on list selection. A different file may be selected than indicated in the File field. - Accepting is enabled based on File field. It's automatically updated when a file is clicked, but the user may input anything there. If the provided path is invalid, accepting is not possible, both with Enter and the Open button (regardless if it's enabled). I checked how Windows causes this. It just never disables the Open button 🤷‍♂️ I guess the Godot's FileDialog could do the same? I'm not sure what's the proper fix otherwise. Accepting and the Open button should be either consistent, or there is no point in disabling the button. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a project 2. Use Scene > Open Scene... 3. See above ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
